name: hexgui
desc: GUI for playing Hex over Hex Text Protocol
why: A GUI for playing Hex against engines over the Hex Text Protocol, a small window into combinatorial game AI.

brief.what_it_is: HexGui is a graphical front end for playing Hex, the two-player connection board game. The homepage README is very short and does not describe the program's features, so the claim that it plays against engines over the Hex Text Protocol comes from the package description and scout notes, not the README. The page shows a Java-style build (an ant build file and a bin/hexgui launcher), with a windows directory and an l4j ant target for building a Windows exe. Nothing on the page describes the board-size options beyond one commit that adds 15x15.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no motivation. The scout notes frame it as a window into combinatorial game AI: a way to watch and play engines that speak the Hex Text Protocol.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism. From the package description, the GUI talks to a separate engine process over the Hex Text Protocol, and the engine does the move selection.

commands_seen.context: README build step ('To build:'), run from the source root. Builds the project with Apache Ant.
README run step ('To run:'), launches the GUI from the bin directory.

brief.install_notes: The README gives only the two commands above. It does not name a Java version, an Ant install, or any engine to play against. Commit history mentions an ant target 'l4j' for producing a Windows exe. Installing via Homebrew is the packager's route and the README says nothing about it. Playing against an AI requires a Hex Text Protocol engine, which the README does not mention or supply.
brief.standout: It is a small, focused GUI aimed at a niche: a Hex board that can be pointed at any engine speaking a plain text protocol, which makes it a practical way to see Hex AI play. It was built by the same authors as the benzene project it lives under.
brief.status: Quiet. SourceForge shows 'Status: Beta'. The file tree's newest entry is src, last changed 2014-01-21 (commit f26689, 'Add 15x15 to list of board sizes.'). The README is dated 10/02/26 (2010-02-26). I saw no recent release or commit.
brief.caveats: The README is minimal and contains no usage guide, screenshots, or engine setup. The homepage is a SourceForge wrapper and the README is the only documentation I could read. The project's last visible commit is over a decade old. Licensing: the repository includes a COPYING file, but I did not open it, so I cannot name the license from what I read.
quotes: Add 15x15 to list of board sizes.
